--- The Materialist Promise Neuroscience made a promise in the late twentieth century, implicitly if not explicitly: give us enough time and enough fMRI machines and we will explain consciousness.
When we understand brains completely, we will understand consciousness completely.
The hard problem will dissolve the way vitalism dissolved when biochemistry explained what "life force" actually was — it was just chemistry.
Knowing which neurons fire when you see red does not explain why there is a subjective experience of redness attached to that firing pattern.
The computation operates on two levels — quantum and classical — unified by a coherence field (the chi field ).
And the parameters of the computation are set by boundary conditions that no theory predicts (the fine-tuning constants).
The chi field makes this formal: consciousness is a term in the coherence integral, and removing it collapses the entire framework.
If you assume that matter is fundamental and consciousness is derivative, you will never explain how matter produces consciousness, because matter doesn't produce consciousness.
Consciousness and matter are two outputs of the same computational process, two projections of the same coherence field, two terms in the same equation.
It sounds like someone trying to smuggle God into the equations through the back door.
It has been there since one thousand nine hundred twenty seven, when the Copenhagen interpretation placed the observer at the center of quantum mechanics.
